{{Short description|Algorithm for the multi-armed bandit problem}}
'''Explore Then Commit''' (ETC) is an algorithm for the [[Multi-armed bandit|multi-armed bandit problem]] focused on finding the best trade-off between exploration and exploitation.

== Multi-armed bandit problem ==

The [[multi-armed bandit problem]] is a [[Sequential game|sequential game]] where one player has to choose at each turn between <math>K</math> actions (arms). Behind every arm <math>a</math> is an unknown distribution <math>\nu_a</math> that lies in a set <math>\mathcal{D}</math> known by the player (for example, <math>\mathcal{D}</math> can be the set of [[Normal distribution|Gaussian distributions]] or [[Bernoulli distribution|Bernoulli distributions]]).

At each turn <math>t</math> the player chooses (pulls) an arm <math>a_t</math>, they then get an observation <math>X_t</math> of the distribution <math>\nu_{a_t}</math>.

=== Regret minimization ===

The goal is to minimize the regret at time <math>T</math> that is defined as
: <math>R_T := \sum_{a=1}^K \Delta_a \mathbb{E}[N_a(T)]</math>
where
* <math>\mu_a := \mathbb{E}[\nu_a]</math> is the mean of arm <math>a</math>
* <math>\mu^* := \max_a \mu_a</math> is the highest mean
* <math>\Delta_a := \mu^* - \mu_a</math>
* <math>N_a(t)</math> is the number of pulls of arm <math>a</math> up to turn <math>t</math>

The player has to find an algorithm that chooses at each turn <math>t</math> which arm to pull based on the previous actions and observations <math>(a_s,X_s)_{s < t}</math> to minimize the regret <math>R_T</math>.

This is a trade-off problem between exploration (finding the arm with the highest mean) and exploitation (playing the arm which is perceived to be the best as much as possible).<ref name="LattimoreSzepesvari2020"/>

== Algorithm ==

[[File:ETCdoublerun.gif|thumb|Two runs of ETC with the same M = 10. On the first run it does manage to find the best arm after the exploration while it does not on the second run]]

The algorithm explores each arm <math>M</math> times. For the rest of the game the algorithm exploits its discoveries by playing the arm with the highest mean. If the horizon <math>T</math> is known, then the number of explorations <math>M</math> can depend on <math>T</math>.

Adaptations of the algorithm exist<ref name="JinXuXiaoGu2021"/> and can be found in the literature for other settings.<ref name="NieAgarwalUmrawalAggarwalQuinn2022"/>

=== Pseudocode ===

 The player chooses M
  '''for''' each arm '''i''' '''do''':
     select arm '''i''' M times
     update empirical mean mu['''i''']
 '''for''' t from MK+1 to T '''do''':
     select arm '''a''' with highest empirical mean mu['''a''']

== Theoretical results ==

[[File:ETCregret.png|thumb|Trade of between exploration (large M) and exploitation (small M) for ETC]]

When all arms are <math>1</math>-sub gaussian, by choosing to explore each arm <math>M</math> times, the regret at time <math>T</math> verify
:<math>
R_T \leq  M \sum_{i = 1}^K \Delta_i + (T - M K) \sum_{i=1}^K \Delta_i \exp\left( -\frac{M \Delta_i^2}{4} \right)
</math><ref name="LattimoreSzepesvari2020"/>

the first term is considered the cost of the exploration
:<math>
M \sum_{i = 1}^K \Delta_i</math>.
The second term is the cost of not having explored enough, leading to a probability of not having an optimal arm as the arm with the highest empirical mean.
:<math>
(T - M K) \sum_{i=1}^K \Delta_i \exp\left( -\frac{M \Delta_i^2}{4} \right)</math>
Increasing <math>M</math> increases the first term while decreasing the second term. The best possible <math>M</math> must depend on the <math>(\Delta_i)_i</math> which is unknown by the player.

For two arms with Gaussian distribution of variance <math>1</math>, it was proved that ETC cannot achieve the asymptotic optimal regret of the Equation of [[Tze Leung Lai|Lai]]-[[Herbert Robbins|Robbins]].<ref name="GarivierKaufmannLattimore2016"/>
